# Plugin API reference

<!-- Generated by docs/src/plugin-api.test.ts. Don't edit this file. Regenerate: bun --bun vitest run docs/src/plugin-api.test.ts -u -->

This page lists what a plugin can import from `@aphelion/plugin-sdk`, for plugin API version 0.2.3. A plugin's manifest names the plugin API versions it works with ([the API range](plugin-manifest.md#the-api-range)). A test generates this page from the types and doc comments in [`packages/plugin-sdk/src`](https://github.com/jcore9/Aphelion/tree/main/packages/plugin-sdk/src) and fails when this page is out of date.

A `z.ZodType<T>` on this page is a [Zod](https://zod.dev/) schema. Its `parse` method checks a value and returns it as a `T`, or throws when the value doesn't match.

## `@aphelion/plugin-sdk`

### `AdapterContext`

What an adapter receives when the bot runner starts it.

```ts
interface AdapterContext {
  readonly bot: {
    readonly id: string;
  };
  readonly folder: string;
  readonly resume: SessionRef | null;
  log(message: string): void;
}
```

- `bot`: The bot the adapter runs for.
- `folder`: The absolute path of the folder the vendor's CLI works in.
- `resume`: The vendor session to resume, or `null` to start a new one.
- `log`: Writes a message to the server's log. Never pass event payloads.

### `AdapterEnvelope`

One event on the wire, with its number and its turn.

```ts
type AdapterEnvelope = {
  seq: number;
  turn: (string & import("zod").$brand<"TurnId">) | null;
  event:
    | { type: "session"; ref: string & import("zod").$brand<"SessionRef"> }
    | { type: "text.delta"; text: string }
    | {
        type: "tool.start";
        call: string & import("zod").$brand<"ToolCallId">;
        tool: string;
        kind: "file.read" | "file.write" | "shell" | "web" | "other";
      }
    | {
        type: "tool.end";
        call: string & import("zod").$brand<"ToolCallId">;
        outcome: "error" | "ok" | "denied" | "cancelled";
      }
    | {
        type: "usage";
        inputTokens: number;
        outputTokens: number;
        cacheReadTokens: number;
        cacheWriteTokens: number;
        costUsd: number | null;
      }
    | {
        type: "error";
        code:
          | "cli-not-found"
          | "cli-exited"
          | "signed-out"
          | "rate-limited"
          | "vendor"
          | "adapter";
      }
    | {
        type: "turn.end";
        reason:
          "error" | "denied" | "cancelled" | "completed" | "limit" | "refused";
      }
    | {
        type: "permission.request";
        request: string & import("zod").$brand<"PermissionRequestId">;
        call: (string & import("zod").$brand<"ToolCallId">) | null;
        tool: string;
        kind: "file.read" | "file.write" | "shell" | "web" | "other";
        pathCount: number;
        hasCommand: boolean;
      }
    | {
        type: "permission.decision";
        request: string & import("zod").$brand<"PermissionRequestId">;
        decision: "allow" | "deny";
        by: "rule" | "policy" | "owner" | "default";
        reason:
          | "shell"
          | "web"
          | "cancelled"
          | "inside-folder"
          | "outside-folder"
          | "unknown-tool"
          | "turn-ended"
          | "timeout"
          | "shutdown"
          | "no-decider"
          | "invalid-request"
          | "duplicate-request"
          | "invalid-decision"
          | "decider-failed";
      };
};
```

### `AdapterEvent`

An event that an adapter yields: `session`, `text.delta`, `tool.start`, `tool.end`, `usage`, `error` or `turn.end`.

```ts
type AdapterEvent =
  | { type: "session"; ref: string & import("zod").$brand<"SessionRef"> }
  | { type: "text.delta"; text: string }
  | {
      type: "tool.start";
      call: string & import("zod").$brand<"ToolCallId">;
      tool: string;
      kind: "file.read" | "file.write" | "shell" | "web" | "other";
    }
  | {
      type: "tool.end";
      call: string & import("zod").$brand<"ToolCallId">;
      outcome: "error" | "ok" | "denied" | "cancelled";
    }
  | {
      type: "usage";
      inputTokens: number;
      outputTokens: number;
      cacheReadTokens: number;
      cacheWriteTokens: number;
      costUsd: number | null;
    }
  | {
      type: "error";
      code:
        | "cli-not-found"
        | "cli-exited"
        | "signed-out"
        | "rate-limited"
        | "vendor"
        | "adapter";
    }
  | {
      type: "turn.end";
      reason:
        "error" | "denied" | "cancelled" | "completed" | "limit" | "refused";
    };
```

### `AdapterSession`

One running conversation with the vendor's CLI.

```ts
interface AdapterSession {
  turn(input: TurnInput, signal: AbortSignal): AsyncIterable<AdapterEvent>;
  close?(): MaybePromise<void>;
}
```

- `turn`: Runs one prompt and yields the turn's events in order, ending with exactly one `turn.end`.
  `signal` aborts when the turn is cancelled or fails. The adapter stops the vendor's work, and may still yield `turn.end` and `tool.end`.
  A `tool.end` may come after `turn.end`, from this stream or from a later turn's stream, for a call that is still running.
- `close`: Closes the vendor's session. The runtime calls it once on shutdown.

### `BotAdapter`

What a bot tool implements: a function from one prompt to a stream of normalized events.

```ts
interface BotAdapter {
  readonly provider: string;
  open(context: AdapterContext): MaybePromise<AdapterSession>;
}
```

- `provider`: The provider's name. It matches the bot's `provider` and the manifest's `contributes.botAdapter.provider`.
- `open`: Opens a session. The runtime calls it once, when the bot runner sends `initialize`.

### `Cleanup`

A function that `start` can return. The SDK calls it once when the plugin shuts down, and logs an error if it throws.
It runs after the event handlers that were still running have finished, or after 3 seconds if one of them is still running.

```ts
type Cleanup = () => MaybePromise<void>;
```

### `ContributionKind`

The names of the lists in a manifest's `contributes`.

```ts
type ContributionKind = "secretSchemes" | "screens";
```

### `Decider`

Answers permission requests. It gets the turn's signal, which aborts on cancel and when the turn ends, and the bot's folder.

```ts
type Decider = (
  request: PermissionRequest,
  signal: AbortSignal,
  context: DeciderContext,
) => MaybePromise<PermissionDecision>;
```

### `DeciderContext`

What a decider knows about the bot it answers for.

```ts
interface DeciderContext {
  readonly folder: string;
}
```

- `folder`: The absolute path of the bot's folder, as the bot runner sent it in `initialize`.

### `HostError`

The error that a call to the host rejects with when the host refuses it, such as `Not granted`.

```ts
class HostError extends Error {
  readonly code: number;
  constructor({ code, message }: RpcError);
}
```

- `code`: The JSON-RPC error code, such as `-32001`. `rpcErrors` lists every code the host sends.
- `constructor`: Makes the error from the error object in the host's reply.

### `ManifestIssue`

One problem that `parsePluginManifest` found.

```ts
type ManifestIssue = {
  field?: string;
  message: string;
};
```

- `field`: The field with the problem, such as `permissions.network[0]`. It is missing when the problem is with the whole manifest.
- `message`: What is wrong with the field, such as `is required`.

### `ManifestResult`

The result of `parsePluginManifest`. It holds the manifest when `ok` is `true`, and the problems when `ok` is `false`.

```ts
type ManifestResult =
  | {
      ok: true;
      manifest: PluginManifest;
    }
  | {
      ok: false;
      issues: ManifestIssue[];
    };
```

### `MaybePromise`

A value, or a promise of one.

```ts
type MaybePromise<T> = T | Promise<T>;
```

### `NetworkReply`

The host's reply to `network.get`.

```ts
interface NetworkReply {
  readonly status: number;
  readonly body: string;
}
```

- `status`: The HTTP status code.
- `body`: The response body as text. The host fails a response whose body is larger than 64 KiB.

### `PermissionDecision`

The answer to one permission request. It covers that request only, never a whole session.

```ts
type PermissionDecision = {
  decision: "allow" | "deny";
  by: "rule" | "policy" | "owner" | "default";
  reason:
    | "shell"
    | "web"
    | "cancelled"
    | "inside-folder"
    | "outside-folder"
    | "unknown-tool"
    | "turn-ended"
    | "timeout"
    | "shutdown"
    | "no-decider"
    | "invalid-request"
    | "duplicate-request"
    | "invalid-decision"
    | "decider-failed";
};
```

### `PermissionKind`

The names of the lists in a manifest's `permissions`.

```ts
type PermissionKind = "events" | "secrets" | "network" | "uiSlots";
```

### `PermissionRequest`

What an adapter asks before a tool runs. `truncated` is true when the adapter cut a path list or a command to fit.

```ts
type PermissionRequest = {
  request: string & import("zod").$brand<"PermissionRequestId">;
  call: (string & import("zod").$brand<"ToolCallId">) | null;
  tool: string;
  kind: "file.read" | "file.write" | "shell" | "web" | "other";
  paths: string[];
  command: string | null;
  truncated: boolean;
};
```

### `PermissionRequestId`

The id of one permission request.

```ts
type PermissionRequestId = string & import("zod").$brand<"PermissionRequestId">;
```

### `PluginContext`

The plugin's connection to the host, which `start` receives.

```ts
interface PluginContext {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly api: string;
  readonly events: {
    subscribe(
      name: string,
      handle: (data: unknown) => MaybePromise<void>,
    ): Promise<void>;
  };
  readonly network: {
    get(url: string): Promise<NetworkReply>;
  };
  readonly secrets: {
    use(operation: string, reference: SecretReference): Promise<void>;
  };
  log(message: string): void;
}
```

- `id`: The plugin's `id`, as the host sent it when it started the plugin.
- `api`: The plugin API version that the host runs, such as `0.2.3`.
- `events`: `subscribe(name, handle)` asks the host for an event, and the SDK then calls `handle` with each event's data each time the host delivers it. The deployed server doesn't publish events yet, so only a test host delivers one.
  Once shutdown starts, the SDK calls no handler for a new event, and every call to the host fails with `the plugin is shutting down`.
  It rejects with a `HostError` when the manifest's `permissions.events` doesn't list the event or the owner hasn't granted it.
- `network`: `get(url)` asks the host to fetch an HTTPS URL that `requestUrl` accepts, from a host in `permissions.network` that the owner granted.
  The SDK sends one network or secret call at a time, so a second call waits until the first one has its reply.
- `secrets`: `use(operation, reference)` asks the host to run a named operation with a secret, such as a signed HTTP call.
  The plugin never receives the secret's value or the operation's result, and the call waits its turn like `network.get`.
  The deployed server runs no secret operations yet, so there a granted call fails with error `-32002`. `createTestHost` can run an operation that a test registers.
- `log`: Writes a message to the plugin's log, which goes to the server's log.

### `PluginIO`

The lines that `runPlugin` reads and writes. `main` builds one from standard input and output.

```ts
interface PluginIO {
  readonly input: AsyncIterable<string>;
  write(line: string): Promise<void>;
  log(message: string): void;
}
```

- `input`: The host's messages, one JSON line for each item.
- `write`: Sends one JSON line to the host, without its line break. The promise settles when the line is written.
- `log`: Writes a message to the log.

### `PluginManifest`

A manifest that `parsePluginManifest` accepted, read-only and with every list filled in.
A list that needs a part the plugin doesn't have is typed as empty, such as `uiSlots` for a plugin with only a server part.

```ts
type PluginManifest =
  | Readonly<
      Omit<
        {
          id: string;
          version: string;
          api: string;
          permissions: {
            events: string[];
            secrets: string[];
            network: string[];
            uiSlots: string[];
          };
          contributes: {
            secretSchemes: string[];
            screens: {
              id: string;
              title: string;
              icon?: string | undefined;
              menuOrder?: number | undefined;
            }[];
            botAdapter?: { provider: string } | undefined;
          };
          $schema?: string | undefined;
          repository?: string | undefined;
          server?: { entry: string } | undefined;
          client?: { entry: string } | undefined;
        },
        "permissions" | "contributes" | ("server" | "client")
      > & { server: { readonly entry: string } } & { client?: never } & {
        permissions: {
          readonly events: readonly string[];
          readonly secrets: readonly string[];
          readonly network: readonly string[];
          readonly uiSlots: readonly never[];
        };
        contributes: {
          readonly secretSchemes: readonly string[];
          readonly screens: readonly never[];
        } & { readonly botAdapter?: Readonly<{ provider: string }> };
      }
    >
  | Readonly<
      Omit<
        {
          id: string;
          version: string;
          api: string;
          permissions: {
            events: string[];
            secrets: string[];
            network: string[];
            uiSlots: string[];
          };
          contributes: {
            secretSchemes: string[];
            screens: {
              id: string;
              title: string;
              icon?: string | undefined;
              menuOrder?: number | undefined;
            }[];
            botAdapter?: { provider: string } | undefined;
          };
          $schema?: string | undefined;
          repository?: string | undefined;
          server?: { entry: string } | undefined;
          client?: { entry: string } | undefined;
        },
        "permissions" | "contributes" | ("server" | "client")
      > & { client: { readonly entry: string } } & { server?: never } & {
        permissions: {
          readonly events: readonly string[];
          readonly secrets: readonly never[];
          readonly network: readonly never[];
          readonly uiSlots: readonly string[];
        };
        contributes: {
          readonly secretSchemes: readonly never[];
          readonly screens: readonly Readonly<{
            id: string;
            title: string;
            icon?: string | undefined;
            menuOrder?: number | undefined;
          }>[];
        } & { readonly botAdapter?: Readonly<{ provider: string }> };
      }
    >
  | Readonly<
      Omit<
        {
          id: string;
          version: string;
          api: string;
          permissions: {
            events: string[];
            secrets: string[];
            network: string[];
            uiSlots: string[];
          };
          contributes: {
            secretSchemes: string[];
            screens: {
              id: string;
              title: string;
              icon?: string | undefined;
              menuOrder?: number | undefined;
            }[];
            botAdapter?: { provider: string } | undefined;
          };
          $schema?: string | undefined;
          repository?: string | undefined;
          server?: { entry: string } | undefined;
          client?: { entry: string } | undefined;
        },
        "permissions" | "contributes" | ("server" | "client")
      > & {
        server: { readonly entry: string };
        client: { readonly entry: string };
      } & {} & {
        permissions: {
          readonly events: readonly string[];
          readonly secrets: readonly string[];
          readonly network: readonly string[];
          readonly uiSlots: readonly string[];
        };
        contributes: {
          readonly secretSchemes: readonly string[];
          readonly screens: readonly Readonly<{
            id: string;
            title: string;
            icon?: string | undefined;
            menuOrder?: number | undefined;
          }>[];
        } & { readonly botAdapter?: Readonly<{ provider: string }> };
      }
    >;
```

### `PluginScreen`

A full page that a plugin's client part declares in `contributes.screens`. The app's menu doesn't list it yet.

```ts
type PluginScreen = PluginManifest["contributes"]["screens"][number];
```

### `RealPath`

Resolves every link in an absolute path that holds no `.` or `..` part.
It resolves to `undefined` when nothing exists at the path, not even a broken link, and rejects on any other failure.

```ts
type RealPath = (path: string) => Promise<string | undefined>;
```

### `RpcError`

A JSON-RPC error object.

```ts
interface RpcError {
  readonly code: number;
  readonly message: string;
}
```

- `code`: The error code, such as `-32001`.
- `message`: A short text that says what went wrong, such as `Not granted`.

### `RpcId`

The id of a JSON-RPC request. A reply carries the id of its request.

```ts
type RpcId = string | number;
```

### `RpcMessage`

One JSON-RPC 2.0 message that `rpcMessageSchema` accepted.

```ts
type RpcMessage =
  | { jsonrpc: "2.0"; id: string | number; method: string; params?: unknown }
  | { jsonrpc: "2.0"; method: string; params?: unknown }
  | { jsonrpc: "2.0"; id: string | number; result: unknown }
  | {
      jsonrpc: "2.0";
      id: string | number | null;
      error: { code: number; message: string; data?: unknown };
    };
```

### `RunAdapterOptions`

What `runAdapter` can be told.

```ts
interface RunAdapterOptions {
  readonly decider?: Decider;
  readonly cancelGraceMs?: number;
  readonly decisionDeadlineMs?: number;
}
```

- `decider`: Answers permission requests. The default is `denyAll`.
- `cancelGraceMs`: How long a cancelled turn has to end by itself before the runtime ends it with `cancelled`, in milliseconds. The default is 5000.
- `decisionDeadlineMs`: How long the decider has to answer, in milliseconds. After that the request is denied with reason `timeout`. The default is no deadline.

### `SecretBackend`

What a secret backend plugin implements for the schemes it lists in `contributes.secretSchemes`. The deployed server doesn't call secret backends yet.

```ts
type SecretBackend = {
  resolve(reference: SecretReference): Promise<string>;
};
```

- `resolve`: Returns the secret's value for a reference, or throws if it can't. The value goes only to the secrets broker.

### `SecretReference`

A secret reference, such as `op://vault/item/field`. It is a scheme, then `://`, then the path.

```ts
type SecretReference = `${string}://${string}`;
```

### `ServerPlugin`

A plugin's server part. Pass it to `main` from `@aphelion/plugin-sdk/stdio`.

```ts
interface ServerPlugin {
  start(context: PluginContext): MaybePromise<void> | MaybePromise<Cleanup>;
}
```

- `start`: The SDK calls `start` once, after it has answered the host's `initialize` request.
  If `start` throws or rejects, the plugin stops with that error.
  At shutdown the SDK waits for `start` to finish before it runs the cleanup that `start` returned.

### `SessionRef`

The vendor's id for a session, which the bot runner saves so the bot can resume it.

```ts
type SessionRef = string & import("zod").$brand<"SessionRef">;
```

### `ToolCallId`

The id of one tool call.

```ts
type ToolCallId = string & import("zod").$brand<"ToolCallId">;
```

### `ToolKind`

What a tool does, in terms that don't depend on the vendor.

```ts
type ToolKind = "file.read" | "file.write" | "shell" | "web" | "other";
```

### `TurnDecision`

What `decide` resolves to. `announced` is true when the runtime put a `permission.decision` event for this request on the stream. It stays in memory and never goes on the wire.

```ts
type TurnDecision = PermissionDecision & {
  readonly announced: boolean;
};
```

### `TurnId`

The id of one turn, the bot's work on one prompt.

```ts
type TurnId = string & import("zod").$brand<"TurnId">;
```

### `TurnInput`

The prompt the bot runner sends for one turn.

```ts
interface TurnInput {
  readonly turn: TurnId;
  readonly text: string;
  readonly decide: (request: PermissionRequest) => Promise<TurnDecision>;
}
```

- `turn`: The turn's id.
- `text`: The prompt, at most 256 KiB.
- `decide`: Asks whether a tool may run in this turn. The runtime puts `permission.request` and `permission.decision` on the stream, so the adapter reports nothing itself.
  It always resolves. A request that is invalid, comes after this turn ended, after a cancel or after shutdown began, or isn't answered in time resolves as `deny`. The ones that can't be asked send no event, and resolve with `announced: false`.
  An adapter may report a tool call as `denied` only when its deny has `announced: true`.

### `adapterApiVersion`

The bot adapter API version that this SDK runs, such as `0.1.0`. A new event or field raises the minor version. A changed or removed one raises the major version.

```ts
const adapterApiVersion: "0.1.0";
```

### `adapterEnvelope`

The Zod schema for the params of the `event` notification: `seq`, the turn's id and the event.
`turn` is `null` only for `session` and for an `error` outside a turn.

```ts

  seq: number;
  turn: (string & import("zod").$brand<"TurnId">) | null;
  event:
    | { type: "session"; ref: string & import("zod").$brand<"SessionRef"> }
    | { type: "text.delta"; text: string }
    | {
        type: "tool.start";
        call: string & import("zod").$brand<"ToolCallId">;
        tool: string;
        kind: "file.read" | "file.write" | "shell" | "web" | "other";
      }
    | {
        type: "tool.end";
        call: string & import("zod").$brand<"ToolCallId">;
        outcome: "error" | "ok" | "denied" | "cancelled";
      }
    | {
        type: "usage";
        inputTokens: number;
        outputTokens: number;
        cacheReadTokens: number;
        cacheWriteTokens: number;
        costUsd: number | null;
      }
    | {
        type: "error";
        code:
          | "cli-not-found"
          | "cli-exited"
          | "signed-out"
          | "rate-limited"
          | "vendor"
          | "adapter";
      }
    | {
        type: "turn.end";
        reason:
          "error" | "denied" | "cancelled" | "completed" | "limit" | "refused";
      }
    | {
        type: "permission.request";
        request: string & import("zod").$brand<"PermissionRequestId">;
        call: (string & import("zod").$brand<"ToolCallId">) | null;
        tool: string;
        kind: "file.read" | "file.write" | "shell" | "web" | "other";
        pathCount: number;
        hasCommand: boolean;
      }
    | {
        type: "permission.decision";
        request: string & import("zod").$brand<"PermissionRequestId">;
        decision: "allow" | "deny";
        by: "rule" | "policy" | "owner" | "default";
        reason:
          | "shell"
          | "web"
          | "cancelled"
          | "inside-folder"
          | "outside-folder"
          | "unknown-tool"
          | "turn-ended"
          | "timeout"
          | "shutdown"
          | "no-decider"
          | "invalid-request"
          | "duplicate-request"
          | "invalid-decision"
          | "decider-failed";
      };
}>;
```

### `adapterEvent`

The Zod schema for an event that an adapter yields. The runtime adds `seq` and `turn`.
No field can hold a command, a path or free text, except the text of `text.delta`.

```ts
const adapterEvent: z.ZodType<
  | { type: "session"; ref: string & import("zod").$brand<"SessionRef"> }
  | { type: "text.delta"; text: string }
  | {
      type: "tool.start";
      call: string & import("zod").$brand<"ToolCallId">;
      tool: string;
      kind: "file.read" | "file.write" | "shell" | "web" | "other";
    }
  | {
      type: "tool.end";
      call: string & import("zod").$brand<"ToolCallId">;
      outcome: "error" | "ok" | "denied" | "cancelled";
    }
  | {
      type: "usage";
      inputTokens: number;
      outputTokens: number;
      cacheReadTokens: number;
      cacheWriteTokens: number;
      costUsd: number | null;
    }
  | {
      type: "error";
      code:
        | "cli-not-found"
        | "cli-exited"
        | "signed-out"
        | "rate-limited"
        | "vendor"
        | "adapter";
    }
  | {
      type: "turn.end";
      reason:
        "error" | "denied" | "cancelled" | "completed" | "limit" | "refused";
    }
>;
```

### `adapterInitializeParams`

The Zod schema for the params of the bot runner's `initialize` request.

```ts
const adapterInitializeParams: z.ZodType<{
  api: string;
  bot: { id: string };
  folder: string;
  resume: (string & import("zod").$brand<"SessionRef">) | null;
}>;
```

### `adapterMethods`

The methods that the bot runner and the adapter send over their JSON lines. `permissionAsk` is reserved for M2.

```ts
const adapterMethods: {
  readonly initialize: "initialize";
  readonly turnStart: "turn.start";
  readonly turnCancel: "turn.cancel";
  readonly shutdown: "shutdown";
  readonly event: "event";
  readonly permissionAsk: "permission.ask";
};
```

### `denyAll`

A `Decider` that denies every request with `by: "default"`.

```ts
const denyAll: Decider;
```

### `eventParams`

The Zod schema for the params of the host's `event` notification.

```ts
const eventParams: z.ZodType<{ name: string; data: unknown }>;
```

### `failure`

Builds a JSON-RPC error reply. The id is `null` when the request couldn't be read.

```ts
const failure: (
  id: RpcId | null,
  error: RpcError,
) => { jsonrpc: string; id: RpcId | null; error: RpcError };
```

### `folderRule`

The fixed rule for a bot before approvals exist. It allows file tools only inside the bot's folder, allows shell commands, and denies web and every other tool.
A path is resolved against the folder, `..` is applied, and every link is followed with `realpath`, so a link inside the folder that points out of it counts as outside.
A path that doesn't exist yet is judged by the nearest folder above it that does.
A pattern such as `src/*.ts` is judged by its fixed part before the first wildcard. A pattern with `..` after a wildcard is denied.
Each answer covers one request.

```ts
function folderRule(realpath: RealPath): Decider;
```

### `initializeParams`

The Zod schema for the params of the host's `initialize` request.

```ts
const initializeParams: z.ZodType<{ api: string; plugin: string }>;
```

### `maxPluginLineBytes`

The most UTF-8 bytes one JSON line may hold, not counting the newline. The limit is 1 MiB.

```ts
const maxPluginLineBytes: number;
```

### `methods`

The JSON-RPC method names that the host and a plugin send.

```ts
const methods: {
  readonly initialize: "initialize";
  readonly event: "event";
  readonly shutdown: "shutdown";
  readonly subscribe: "events.subscribe";
  readonly networkGet: "network.get";
  readonly secretsUse: "secrets.use";
};
```

### `networkGetParams`

The Zod schema for the params of `network.get`. The URL is at most 4096 characters.

```ts
const networkGetParams: z.ZodType<{ url: string }>;
```

### `networkReply`

The Zod schema for the result of `network.get`.

```ts
const networkReply: z.ZodType<{ status: number; body: string }>;
```

### `notification`

Builds a JSON-RPC notification. It leaves out `params` when they are `undefined`.

```ts
const notification: (
  method: string,
  params?: unknown,
) =>
  | { jsonrpc: string; method: string; params?: never }
  | { jsonrpc: string; method: string; params: {} | null };
```

### `parsePluginManifest`

Checks the parsed JSON of `aphelion-plugin.json`, including its API range. It returns the problems instead of throwing.

```ts
function parsePluginManifest(data: unknown): ManifestResult;
```

### `permissionDecision`

The Zod schema for the answer to a permission request. `reason` is one of a fixed list of codes, such as `outside-folder`, never text.

```ts
const permissionDecision: z.ZodType<{
  decision: "allow" | "deny";
  by: "rule" | "policy" | "owner" | "default";
  reason:
    | "shell"
    | "web"
    | "cancelled"
    | "inside-folder"
    | "outside-folder"
    | "unknown-tool"
    | "turn-ended"
    | "timeout"
    | "shutdown"
    | "no-decider"
    | "invalid-request"
    | "duplicate-request"
    | "invalid-decision"
    | "decider-failed";
}>;
```

### `permissionRequest`

The Zod schema for a permission request as the adapter hands it to `decide`. The paths and the command stay in memory and never go into an event.

```ts
const permissionRequest: z.ZodType<{
  request: string & import("zod").$brand<"PermissionRequestId">;
  call: (string & import("zod").$brand<"ToolCallId">) | null;
  tool: string;
  kind: "file.read" | "file.write" | "shell" | "web" | "other";
  paths: string[];
  command: string | null;
  truncated: boolean;
}>;
```

### `permissionRequestId`

The Zod schema for a permission request's id. The adapter picks it. It has the same form as a tool call's id.

```ts
const permissionRequestId: z.ZodType<
  string & import("zod").$brand<"PermissionRequestId">
>;
```

### `pluginApiVersion`

The plugin API version that this SDK and the host run. A manifest's `api` range must include it.

```ts
const pluginApiVersion: "0.2.3";
```

### `pluginLineFits`

Whether `line`, without its newline, fits in `maxPluginLineBytes` as UTF-8.

```ts
function pluginLineFits(line: string): boolean;
```

### `pluginManifestFile`

The name of the manifest file in a plugin's folder.

```ts
const pluginManifestFile: "aphelion-plugin.json";
```

### `pluginManifestSchema`

The Zod schema for `aphelion-plugin.json`, whose fields [the plugin manifest reference](plugin-manifest.md) lists.
It fills in empty lists and checks that `api` is a valid version range, but not that the range includes `pluginApiVersion`. `parsePluginManifest` checks both.

```ts
const pluginManifestSchema: z.ZodType<{
  id: string;
  version: string;
  api: string;
  permissions: {
    events: string[];
    secrets: string[];
    network: string[];
    uiSlots: string[];
  };
  contributes: {
    secretSchemes: string[];
    screens: {
      id: string;
      title: string;
      icon?: string | undefined;
      menuOrder?: number | undefined;
    }[];
    botAdapter?: { provider: string } | undefined;
  };
  $schema?: string | undefined;
  repository?: string | undefined;
  server?: { entry: string } | undefined;
  client?: { entry: string } | undefined;
}>;
```

### `releaseArchiveName`

The name of the release asset that holds the plugin's `dist/` folder, as a plain ustar archive.

```ts
const releaseArchiveName: "aphelion-plugin.tar";
```

### `releaseBundleName`

The name of the release asset that holds the GitHub artifact attestation for `releaseArchiveName`.

```ts
const releaseBundleName: "aphelion-plugin.tar.sigstore.json";
```

### `request`

Builds a JSON-RPC request.

```ts
const request: (
  id: RpcId,
  method: string,
  params: unknown,
) => { jsonrpc: string; id: RpcId; method: string; params: unknown };
```

### `requestUrl`

Checks a URL's form for `network.get`, and returns the URL, or `undefined` if the form is wrong.
The URL must use `https:`, a hostname with a dot and no dot at the end, and the default port, with no user name, password or text after a `#`, and not an IP address. `network.get` also refuses a URL longer than 4096 characters and a host that isn't granted.

```ts
function requestUrl(text: string): URL | undefined;
```

### `rpcErrors`

The errors that the host and the adapter runtime reply with, by name.
[The plugin reference](plugins.md#errors) says when the host sends each one.
`busy` and `turnEnded` also answer a bot adapter's `turn.start`, as [the bot adapter reference](bot-adapters.md#what-the-runtime-does) says.

```ts
const rpcErrors: {
  readonly parse: { readonly code: -32700; readonly message: "Parse error" };
  readonly invalidRequest: {
    readonly code: -32600;
    readonly message: "Invalid request";
  };
  readonly methodNotFound: {
    readonly code: -32601;
    readonly message: "Method not found";
  };
  readonly invalidParams: {
    readonly code: -32602;
    readonly message: "Invalid params";
  };
  readonly notGranted: {
    readonly code: -32001;
    readonly message: "Not granted";
  };
  readonly noSecretOperations: {
    readonly code: -32002;
    readonly message: "The host doesn't offer secret operations yet";
  };
  readonly operationFailed: {
    readonly code: -32003;
    readonly message: "Operation failed";
  };
  readonly busy: {
    readonly code: -32004;
    readonly message: "Operation in progress";
  };
  readonly turnEnded: {
    readonly code: -32005;
    readonly message: "Turn already ended";
  };
};
```

### `rpcMessageSchema`

The Zod schema for one JSON-RPC 2.0 message: a request, a notification, a success reply or an error reply. It refuses a field that the message type doesn't have.

```ts
const rpcMessageSchema: z.ZodType<
  | { jsonrpc: "2.0"; id: string | number; method: string; params?: unknown }
  | { jsonrpc: "2.0"; method: string; params?: unknown }
  | { jsonrpc: "2.0"; id: string | number; result: unknown }
  | {
      jsonrpc: "2.0";
      id: string | number | null;
      error: { code: number; message: string; data?: unknown };
    }
>;
```

### `runAdapter`

Runs a bot adapter on the given lines until the bot runner sends `shutdown` or closes its input. Most adapters call `mainAdapter` instead.
The runtime numbers events, runs one turn at a time, checks every event with Zod before it sends it, settles each permission request exactly once, and cancels a turn that doesn't end.
It rejects when writing a line fails or when the adapter's `open` fails.

```ts
function runAdapter(
  adapter: BotAdapter,
  io: PluginIO,
  options?: RunAdapterOptions,
): Promise<void>;
```

### `secretsUseParams`

The Zod schema for the params of `secrets.use`. The operation name is at most 128 characters, and the reference at most 1024.

```ts
const secretsUseParams: z.ZodType<{ operation: string; reference: string }>;
```

### `sessionRef`

The Zod schema for the vendor's session id. The id is opaque: 1 to 256 printable ASCII characters, with no space and no `/`, so it can't be a path or a command with arguments. Vendor session ids are UUID-like.

```ts
const sessionRef: z.ZodType<string & import("zod").$brand<"SessionRef">>;
```

### `streamEvent`

The Zod schema for every event that leaves the bot process. It adds `permission.request` and `permission.decision`, which only the runtime sends.

```ts
const streamEvent: z.ZodType<
  | { type: "session"; ref: string & import("zod").$brand<"SessionRef"> }
  | { type: "text.delta"; text: string }
  | {
      type: "tool.start";
      call: string & import("zod").$brand<"ToolCallId">;
      tool: string;
      kind: "file.read" | "file.write" | "shell" | "web" | "other";
    }
  | {
      type: "tool.end";
      call: string & import("zod").$brand<"ToolCallId">;
      outcome: "error" | "ok" | "denied" | "cancelled";
    }
  | {
      type: "usage";
      inputTokens: number;
      outputTokens: number;
      cacheReadTokens: number;
      cacheWriteTokens: number;
      costUsd: number | null;
    }
  | {
      type: "error";
      code:
        | "cli-not-found"
        | "cli-exited"
        | "signed-out"
        | "rate-limited"
        | "vendor"
        | "adapter";
    }
  | {
      type: "turn.end";
      reason:
        "error" | "denied" | "cancelled" | "completed" | "limit" | "refused";
    }
  | {
      type: "permission.request";
      request: string & import("zod").$brand<"PermissionRequestId">;
      call: (string & import("zod").$brand<"ToolCallId">) | null;
      tool: string;
      kind: "file.read" | "file.write" | "shell" | "web" | "other";
      pathCount: number;
      hasCommand: boolean;
    }
  | {
      type: "permission.decision";
      request: string & import("zod").$brand<"PermissionRequestId">;
      decision: "allow" | "deny";
      by: "rule" | "policy" | "owner" | "default";
      reason:
        | "shell"
        | "web"
        | "cancelled"
        | "inside-folder"
        | "outside-folder"
        | "unknown-tool"
        | "turn-ended"
        | "timeout"
        | "shutdown"
        | "no-decider"
        | "invalid-request"
        | "duplicate-request"
        | "invalid-decision"
        | "decider-failed";
    }
>;
```

### `subscribeParams`

The Zod schema for the params of `events.subscribe`. The event name is at most 128 characters.

```ts
const subscribeParams: z.ZodType<{ event: string }>;
```

### `success`

Builds a JSON-RPC success reply.

```ts
const success: (
  id: RpcId,
  result: unknown,
) => { jsonrpc: string; id: RpcId; result: unknown };
```

### `toolCallId`

The Zod schema for a tool call's id. The adapter picks it, usually the vendor's own id. It is 1 to 128 letters, digits, `_`, `.`, `:` or `-`.

```ts
const toolCallId: z.ZodType<string & import("zod").$brand<"ToolCallId">>;
```

### `toolKind`

The Zod schema for a tool's kind. The adapter maps each vendor tool to one kind, and a tool it doesn't know is `other`.

```ts
const toolKind: z.ZodType<
  "file.read" | "file.write" | "shell" | "web" | "other"
>;
```

### `turnCancelParams`

The Zod schema for the params of the bot runner's `turn.cancel` request.

```ts
const turnCancelParams: z.ZodType<{
  turn: string & import("zod").$brand<"TurnId">;
}>;
```

### `turnId`

The Zod schema for a turn's id. The bot runner picks it. It is 1 to 64 letters, digits, `_` or `-`.

```ts
const turnId: z.ZodType<string & import("zod").$brand<"TurnId">>;
```

### `turnStartParams`

The Zod schema for the params of the bot runner's `turn.start` request. The prompt is at most 256 KiB.

```ts
const turnStartParams: z.ZodType<{
  turn: string & import("zod").$brand<"TurnId">;
  text: string;
}>;
```

## `@aphelion/plugin-sdk/runtime`

### `runPlugin`

Runs a plugin on the given lines until the host sends `shutdown` or closes its input. It then reads no more events, waits up to 3 seconds for event handlers that are still running, and runs the plugin's cleanup.
It rejects when the plugin's `start` fails before shutdown begins, or when reading or writing a line fails while the plugin runs. A `start` that fails after shutdown has begun is only logged. Most plugins call `main` instead.

```ts
function runPlugin(plugin: ServerPlugin, io: PluginIO): Promise<void>;
```

## `@aphelion/plugin-sdk/stdio`

### `RunAdapterOptions`

What `runAdapter` can be told.

```ts
interface RunAdapterOptions {
  readonly decider?: Decider;
  readonly cancelGraceMs?: number;
  readonly decisionDeadlineMs?: number;
}
```

- `decider`: Answers permission requests. The default is `denyAll`.
- `cancelGraceMs`: How long a cancelled turn has to end by itself before the runtime ends it with `cancelled`, in milliseconds. The default is 5000.
- `decisionDeadlineMs`: How long the decider has to answer, in milliseconds. After that the request is denied with reason `timeout`. The default is no deadline.

### `main`

Runs a plugin on standard input and output, and exits the process when the plugin stops, with code 0, or 1 after an error.
It drops a line from the host that is longer than 1 MiB, and logs that it did.

```ts
function main(plugin: ServerPlugin): void;
```

### `mainAdapter`

Runs a bot adapter on standard input and output, and exits the process when the adapter stops, with code 0, or 1 after an error.
It drops a line from the bot runner that is longer than 1 MiB, and logs that it did.

```ts
function mainAdapter(adapter: BotAdapter, options?: RunAdapterOptions): void;
```

## `@aphelion/plugin-sdk/testing`

### `AdapterHarness`

A fake bot runner that talks to an adapter's runtime over JSON lines, and keeps what it receives.

```ts
interface AdapterHarness {
  readonly events: readonly AdapterEnvelope[];
  readonly logs: readonly string[];
  readonly problems: readonly string[];
  readonly done: Promise<void>;
  initialize(resume?: string | null): Promise<AdapterReply>;
  startTurn(turn: string, text: string): Promise<AdapterReply>;
  cancel(turn: string): Promise<AdapterReply>;
  shutdown(): Promise<AdapterReply>;
  untilEvent(
    match: (event: AdapterEnvelope) => boolean,
  ): Promise<AdapterEnvelope>;
}
```

- `events`: The events that the adapter sent, in order.
- `logs`: The messages that the runtime logged.
- `problems`: Lines the runtime sent that the harness couldn't read, such as an event that fails its schema. A good test leaves this empty.
- `done`: Settles when the runtime stops: it resolves after `shutdown` and rejects when the runtime fails.
- `initialize`: Sends `initialize` for a bot called `bot-1` in the folder from the options, with no session to resume unless `resume` says otherwise.
- `startTurn`: Sends `turn.start`. The reply comes when the runtime accepts the turn, not when the turn ends.
- `cancel`: Sends `turn.cancel`.
- `shutdown`: Sends `shutdown` and waits for the reply.
- `untilEvent`: Resolves with the first event that `match` accepts, including one that has arrived already.

### `AdapterReply`

The bot adapter's reply to a request, which is a result or an error.

```ts
type AdapterReply =
  | {
      readonly result: unknown;
    }
  | {
      readonly error: RpcError;
    };
```

### `CallOutcome`

The test host's answer to a request, which is a result or an error.

```ts
type CallOutcome =
  | {
      readonly result: unknown;
    }
  | {
      readonly error: {
        readonly code: number;
        readonly message: string;
      };
    };
```

### `FakeAdapter`

A `BotAdapter` that runs a script, and keeps what the runtime gave it.

```ts
interface FakeAdapter extends BotAdapter {
  readonly contexts: readonly AdapterContext[];
  readonly inputs: readonly TurnInput[];
  readonly signals: readonly AbortSignal[];
  readonly answers: readonly TurnDecision[];
  readonly closed: boolean;
}
```

- `contexts`: The contexts that `open` received.
- `inputs`: The turns the runtime started, in order.
- `signals`: The signal of each turn, in order.
- `answers`: The answers to the `ask` steps, in order.
- `closed`: Whether the runtime has called `close`.

### `FakeScript`

A script's turns. The first turn that the runtime starts runs the first list of steps, the second turn the second list, and so on. A turn past the end of the script yields nothing.

```ts
type FakeScript = readonly (readonly FakeStep[])[];
```

### `FakeSecretOperation`

A secret operation that the test host runs for `secrets.use`.

```ts
interface FakeSecretOperation {
  readonly reference: SecretReference;
  readonly host: string;
  run(pluginId: string): MaybePromise<unknown>;
}
```

- `reference`: The secret reference that the plugin must name, and that the plugin needs a grant for.
- `host`: The hostname that the operation sends to. The plugin needs a network grant for it.
- `run`: Runs the operation with the plugin's id. The plugin never sees what it returns or throws, and the call fails after 5 seconds.

### `FakeStep`

One step of a fake turn. The fake adapter runs a turn's steps in order.

```ts
type FakeStep =
  | {
      readonly emit: AdapterEvent;
    }
  | {
      readonly emitRaw: unknown;
    }
  | {
      readonly ask: PermissionRequest;
    }
  | {
      readonly wait: PromiseLike<unknown>;
    }
  | {
      readonly waitForAbort: true;
    }
  | {
      readonly hang: true;
    }
  | {
      readonly throws: true;
    };
```

### `Grant`

A permission that the owner granted, for `TestHost.setGrants`.

```ts
interface Grant {
  readonly kind: "events" | "network" | "secrets";
  readonly name: string;
}
```

- `kind`: The manifest list in `permissions` that the permission is in.
- `name`: The event name, hostname or secret reference.

### `HarnessOptions`

What `startAdapter` and `runTurn` can be told: the runtime's options and the bot's folder.

```ts
interface HarnessOptions extends RunAdapterOptions {
  readonly folder?: string;
}
```

- `folder`: The folder that `initialize` sends. The default is `/work`.

### `HostCall`

One request that the plugin sent to the test host.

```ts
interface HostCall {
  readonly method: string;
  readonly params: unknown;
  readonly outcome: CallOutcome;
}
```

- `method`: The JSON-RPC method, such as `network.get`.
- `params`: The params that the plugin sent.
- `outcome`: The test host's answer.

### `StreamViolation`

One rule that a stream broke.

```ts
interface StreamViolation {
  readonly rule: number;
  readonly message: string;
}
```

- `rule`: The rule's number, from 1 to 7, or 0 for an event that isn't valid. The rules are numbered as [the bot adapter reference](bot-adapters.md#rules-a-stream-follows) numbers them.
- `message`: What broke the rule. It names ids and numbers only, never text from the stream.

### `TestHost`

A fake host for a plugin's tests. It checks grants, request shapes and secret operations the way the real host does. Network replies are fixtures from `respondToGet`, not real requests. It does no DNS lookup, public-address check or TLS.
Unlike the real host, it can run secret operations that a test registers with `registerSecretOperation`.

```ts
interface TestHost {
  setGrants(grants: readonly Grant[]): void;
  respondToGet(url: string, respond: () => MaybePromise<NetworkReply>): void;
  registerSecretOperation(name: string, operation: FakeSecretOperation): void;
  start(plugin: ServerPlugin): Promise<void>;
  publish(name: string, data: unknown): Promise<void>;
  stop(): Promise<void>;
  readonly logs: readonly string[];
  readonly calls: readonly HostCall[];
}
```

- `setGrants`: Sets what the owner granted, replacing earlier grants. A grant counts only when the manifest also lists the permission.
- `respondToGet`: Sets the fixture reply to `network.get` for one URL. Nothing is fetched. A URL with no reply, a reply that takes more than 5 seconds, and a body larger than 64 KiB fail with `Operation failed`.
- `registerSecretOperation`: Adds a named operation for `secrets.use`. While none is registered, `secrets.use` with a granted reference fails with error `-32002`.
- `start`: Starts the plugin and resolves when its `start` has finished, or rejects when `start` fails. A test host starts one plugin only.
- `publish`: Sends an event to the plugin and resolves when its handler has finished.
  It rejects when the encoded event line is longer than 1 MiB, as the real host does, and sends nothing.
  It sends nothing and resolves at once when the plugin isn't running, hasn't subscribed, or isn't granted the event, and from the moment `stop` is called.
- `stop`: Sends `shutdown` and resolves when the plugin has stopped. The SDK first waits up to 3 seconds for handlers that are still running, then runs the plugin's cleanup.
  A second call resolves when the first one does.
- `logs`: The messages that the plugin and the SDK logged, in order.
- `calls`: The requests that the plugin sent, with the answers, in the order the test host answered them.

### `TurnRun`

What `runTurn` returns.

```ts
interface TurnRun {
  readonly reply: AdapterReply;
  readonly events: readonly AdapterEnvelope[];
  readonly logs: readonly string[];
  readonly problems: readonly string[];
}
```

- `reply`: The reply to `turn.start`. An error reply means the runtime refused the turn, and then nothing else ran.
- `events`: Every event that the adapter sent, in order.
- `logs`: The messages that the runtime logged.
- `problems`: Lines the harness couldn't read.

### `checkStream`

Checks the events of one bot process against the seven rules of [the bot adapter reference](bot-adapters.md#rules-a-stream-follows).
It checks each event with the same Zod schema the runtime uses, so a caller needn't validate first. An event that fails it is reported as rule 0 and skipped by the other rules.
It returns the broken rules, and an empty list when the stream is good. Pass a stream that has finished: a turn without a `turn.end` breaks rule 3.

```ts
function checkStream(events: readonly unknown[]): StreamViolation[];
```

### `createTestHost`

Makes a test host for a plugin's manifest, with nothing granted. It throws when the manifest is invalid or has no server part.

```ts
function createTestHost(manifestData: unknown): TestHost;
```

### `fakeAdapter`

Makes an adapter that runs `script`. Its provider is `fake` unless `provider` says otherwise.

```ts
function fakeAdapter(script: FakeScript, provider?: string): FakeAdapter;
```

### `runTurn`

Runs one turn the way the bot runner does: `initialize`, `turn.start`, waiting for `turn.end`, then `shutdown`.
`turn` is `t1` unless the options say otherwise, and `text` is `hello`.

```ts
function runTurn(
  adapter: BotAdapter,
  options?: HarnessOptions & { turn?: string; text?: string },
): Promise<TurnRun>;
```

### `startAdapter`

```ts
function startAdapter(
  adapter: BotAdapter,
  options?: HarnessOptions,
): AdapterHarness;
```
